note: A salaried barber manager at a state prison and a Marine Corps veteran — employed, not a business owner or physician, so 'successful' fails on the stated test despite obvious capability and a shop-ownership path with an investor ahead of him. Income fails on the record: a recent pay cut, a nine-person household, and an inability to carry $650/month, $433/month or even $200/month without waiting for paychecks to stabilise. Good-to-great fails — he opened with 'I'm overweight, but I want to lose weight', which is close to the exact phrasing the stated ICP uses to describe who they do not take. Health is genuinely the neglected corner rather than a crisis, and the deconditioned exclusion does not cleanly apply: no weight figure was given and he is the opposite of gym-averse, having spent four years in the Marine Corps and already owning a kettlebell. Worth flagging for the rollup: the rep used the 'business owners, athletes, CEOs, executives, people like yourself' framing twice to a prison barber manager, and the prospect never questioned it — the same script language that Brad Custis pushed back on the day before.
